absent: Enabled kallsyms lookup, formatting and iteration semantics are absent.
Debugger command implementations, polling loop and console interaction are absent.
Remote-debug wire protocol, exception entry and single-step mechanics are absent.
Probe insertion, single-stepping, optimization and ftrace integration internals are absent.
Module loading, version enforcement and naming limits beyond the length constant are absent.
Log formatting, index wrapping and message-source trapping details are absent.
Locking for debugger flags, breakpoint tables and blacklist mutation is absent.

findings.text: Unavailable symbol database still exposes lookup by name, lookup of size and offset, lookup by address, several formatted symbol and backtrace printers, single-name resolution and per-symbol iteration helpers.

Disabled symbol behaviour is neutral: numeric lookups yield zero or null, printers produce an empty output and zero length, single-name resolution reports a range error, and iteration helpers report operation not supported.
Instruction-pointer printer accepts a log level and address and forwards them to kernel logging with both raw and symbolic formatting.
Kernel logging entry is a variadic macro that routes format calls through an index wrapper around the core log implementation.

Debugger permission model uses single-bit values for global enable, memory and register access, inspection, flow control, signalling, reboot and always-safe, with a mask over user bits, a shift separating no-argument variants, and two high repeat bits.
Debugger command entry associates a name with a handler function, usage and help strings, a minimum unique prefix length, behaviour flags, and intrusive list linkage.
Debugger limits fix a small maximum for polled functions and sixteen as the maximum argument count per command invocation.

Debugger status codes are small negative integers covering missing command, argument and parsing problems, environment errors, unimplemented operation, resource exhaustion, allocation failure, breakpoint and debug-register limits, duplicate or missing breakpoints, mode and length errors, bad register, cpu, address and permission.

Global debugger state is a bitmask with bits for early entry, catastrophic event, interrupted command, suppression of cross-cpu signalling, and several console or keyboard unavailability conditions, accessed through test, set and clear helpers.

Debugger entry reasons distinguish initial entry, slave entry, breakpoint, debug fault, oops, cpu switch, keyboard, nonmaskable interrupt, recursion, single step and system nonmaskable interrupt; message source distinguishes internal versus trapped log output; initialization progresses through uninitialized, early and full.
When the debugger is unavailable, formatted printing, initialization and command registration become no-ops reporting success or false, and symbol walking yields no result.
Task-to-cpu helper clamps out-of-range values to zero; enabled cpu-local print check compares a stored cpu against the current processor; fallback variant always reports false.

Remote-debug breakpoint record pairs an address with saved instruction bytes, a type and a state; register descriptor triples name, size and offset; architecture operations cover software and hardware breakpoint management and correction; transport operations cover character IO, lifecycle and exception hooks plus console binding.
Remote-debug limits define zero architectural registers in this configuration, a large software breakpoint capacity and an indicator that hardware breakpoint support is present.
Breakpoint types separate software, hardware, write watch, read watch, access watch and poke variants; lifecycle states progress through undefined, removed, set and active.

Master-debugger test is true only with interrupts disabled on the active debug cpu when enabled, otherwise constant false; late init, panic hook, init-memory release and nonmaskable-interrupt callback become empty or fixed-value fallbacks; blocklist check is either delegated or constantly false.

Probe descriptor chains through hash and list links, counts missed hits, locates a target address with optional symbolic name plus offset, stores pre and post handlers, preserves the replaced opcode and a copied instruction, and carries status flags.
Probe execution uses low bits for active hit, single-step, reentry and single-step completion; lifecycle flags mark gone, disabled, optimized, ftrace-backed and entry-point probes.
Flag helpers report gone, disabled-or-gone, optimized and ftrace-backed conditions from the status word.

Return-probe holder references a probe plus an object pool; return probe extends a base probe with return and entry handlers, activity limits, miss count and data size with alternative backends; instance carries backend-specific linkage and trailing data; blacklist structures record address ranges and named points.
Return-probe per-instance data is capped at a four-kilobyte maximum.

Accessors for owning probe and return address, trampoline identity tests and return-address search select between rethook-backed, trampoline-address comparison and constant false or zero fallbacks according to build configuration; trampoline handler brackets delegated handling with busy marking.

Instruction-slot cache holds allocation callbacks, a page symbol, a page list, slot size and garbage count; optimized probe extends a base probe with an optimization queue link and architecture-specific optimized instruction; cache operation macros provide get, free and address-membership helpers or a constant-false fallback.

Slot-cache operations are serialized by the cache mutex; probe status word is stable under the global probe mutex after registration; per-cpu current-probe and control-block accesses assume cpu-local or non-preemptible context.

When probing is unavailable, registration and enable operations report operation not supported, unregistration and task flush and optimizer wait and ftrace teardown become empty, address queries return null or false, and kallsym lookup reports range error.
Page-fault helper must only delegate to fault handling for kernel-mode, non-preemptible faults with a running probe when probing is compiled in; otherwise it returns false without side effects.
Module version record pairs a checksum with a fixed-length name buffer sized by the module-name length constant.
Headers use include guards to prevent multiple inclusion.
